newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says may restart Heidrun Monday.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says may restart Heidrun Monday.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Sunday oil production may resume on Monday at the 250,000 barrels per day Heidrun oilfield, which was hit by a technical snag last week.
Output was shut in at 0800 GMT on Wednesday after the flare tip fell off the platform.

"We hope to get back to production hopefully tomorrow," Statoil spokesman Hogne Hognseth said. "We can use the old flare tip, but some work needs to be done to readjust the tip to its position. We are also dependent on the weather."
The flare tip, a safety measure for releasing pressure in the processing facilities, was picked up by a ship later on Wednesday.
Latest production figures from Statoil showed that Heidrun produced 249,738 barrels of crude on Tuesday.
